claims.text: The initial material is a near-equimolar, rare-earth-free Ni-Fe-Co-Cr-based disordered FCC high-entropy alloy.
Conventionally processed baseline material has a broad distribution of local magnetic exchange interactions.
Atomic-scale chemical homogeneity governs the strength of the low-field magnetocaloric response in disordered FCC high-entropy alloys.
The proposed controlled intervention is addition of approximately 3–5 at.% of an FCC-metal dopant followed by standardized annealing.
Cu or Ag are plausible structural tuning dopants for Ni-Fe-Co-Cr-based high-entropy alloys.
Addition of 3–5 at.% Cu or Ag followed by annealing promotes chemical homogenization.
The hypothesis is to be tested near an approximately room-temperature magnetic transition under fields of about 1 T or less.
Narrower XRD peaks and more uniform lattice parameters evidence a reduced distribution of local magnetic exchange interactions.
The FCC dopant diffuses uniformly during annealing.
Uniform dopant diffusion reduces chemical inhomogeneity.
Doping and annealing reduce local lattice distortions.
Greater chemical homogeneity produces a narrower distribution of magnetic exchange energies.
A narrower distribution of exchange energies sharpens the second-order magnetic transition.
The doped and annealed material will have a more sharply peaked magnetic entropy change than the undoped baseline at low field.
The doped and annealed material will have lower magnetic hysteresis losses than the undoped baseline.
The doped and annealed material will maintain or improve heat-transfer performance.
The doped and annealed material will maintain or improve mechanical performance.
The undoped baseline has a broader magnetic transition and wider magnetic-entropy-change peak.
The proposed mechanism should apply only while FCC structure and high-entropy-alloy characteristics are preserved, and may fail after excessive doping, phase change, or defect introduction.
Failure to obtain statistically significant entropy-peak sharpening together with reduced hysteresis and maintained or improved thermal and mechanical performance would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as potentially as-cast or conventionally processed, whereas the falsification design requires all samples to undergo identical processing including standardized annealing. An as-cast baseline would confound dopant effects with annealing effects.
